transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you in to see me?
I came in because I keep thinking it might be better if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes… I feel like dying would be a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and my crew.
Could you tell me more about what happened with your crew?

Things started going wrong, and I feel like it was because of me. My husband got worse, the crew lost work, and there were problems in clients’ homes. I keep thinking I poisoned everything I touched. Like I ruined it all, and I deserve whatever happens to me because of it.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or empty most of the day?
I’m not sure. I’ve been feeling pretty bad about myself, but I don’t know if I’d call it sad all day.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you usually enjoy doing?
Yeah. I used to paint, cook big meals, run before work, go to theater rehearsals. Now it all just feels like chores from somebody else’s life. I don’t really care if I miss any of it.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or hyperactive?
I don’t think so. I can’t remember having a stretch where I felt unusually energized or really up like that.
Have you ever had another time in your life when you felt this way, losing interest in things and feeling so down on yourself?

Yeah, I guess I have. It’s that same thing where painting or cooking, even running before work or going to rehearsal—it all feels like work I don’t care about anymore. Like it belongs to somebody else, not me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

Yeah. I hear a man’s voice sometimes, like he’s behind me at a job site or in my kitchen. He’ll say things like, “You missed it,” or “Everyone knows.” It sounds clear, like somebody’s right there, but when I turn around there’s nobody.
Have you ever heard that voice at times when your mood was completely fine and you weren't feeling down or guilty?

Yes. There was a few-week stretch where I was getting up, eating a little better, and not crying all day. But I still heard him at work, and I was still convinced the clients and suppliers were tracking me.
